name: ContreeBackend
logic_name: Stateless Contree MCP adapter for immutable image execution

test_list.description: Connection accepts the exact pinned upstream MCP tool inventory and validates the critical run, rsync, image, file, and operation schemas before exposing typed calls.

Typed calls apply finite input/output and fan-out bounds, retain each source image and directory_state_id, and return each immutable result image or pending operation identity without conflating branches.
Configuration rejects non-loopback sidecars and local-to-remote sync without explicit egress consent before any MCP call.
Secrets are never included in debug/error output, tool responses are bounded before typed decoding, and malformed or oversized output fails closed.
Cancellation stops the local request and invokes the upstream cancellation tool for each operation id created and owned by the cancelled call.
Sync requests can transfer only paths explicitly present in the existing storage sync plan after secret and policy filtering.
The checked-in synthetic MCP fixture documents the exact upstream source revision and rejects missing, extra, or shape-drifted advertised tools.

inputs.name: endpoint
inputs.description: Explicit loopback streamable-HTTP endpoint for the supervised contree-mcp sidecar.

inputs.name: request
inputs.description: Bounded command, selected immutable image, optional directory_state_id and explicit run options matching the verified upstream schema.

inputs.name: sync
inputs.description: Existing storage sync plan projected to an allowlisted, secret-filtered transfer set with explicit egress consent.

inputs.name: cancellation
inputs.description: Structured local cancellation; any detached upstream operation remains explicitly owned and is cancelled before return.

output_type: ContreeRunOutcome / typed inspection and operation results
output_description: Stateless immutable-image run outcomes with exact source and branch identity, or typed pending operation identities; no persistent SDK SandboxBackend create/exec/destroy semantics are claimed.
